comments.body:
Implementation evidence — Gerrit change 1951 (Change-Id I026ad4ca58516df192a4046a3262acef7e87e90f), commit 6451d3ff02.

DUPLICATE NOTE: the plan-review overlap detector flagged this ticket as `duplicates` 039b-d179-b669-4439 (classless-dainty-lamprey, confidence 0.82), which shares the title and both file-impact paths and landed the first pass as a79ed876b0. `rebar link 039b-d179-b669-4439 decagonal-indisposed-tamarin duplicates` was refused because the source ticket is closed, so the relation is recorded here instead. This change covers only the residual work that 039b left on main; it does not re-do 039b's slow-progress/read-retry repair.

WINDOWS — old -> new (all test-only; production defaults byte-unchanged at 120s call / 3s grace / 2s drain / 10s low-speed window):
- test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py, blanket autouse `_short_timeout`: REBAR_ACLI_TIMEOUT=1 + 1s grace + 1s drain, applied to the WHOLE module -> deleted. Replaced by two opt-in fixtures: `real_child` (0.2s call / 0.1s grace / 0.1s drain) for the six tests whose fake child must HANG, and `completing_child_timeout` (30s) for test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff, whose two fake children must COMPLETE. That test previously inherited the 1s ceiling as a pass condition — a latent load flake in the opposite direction, which merely shrinking a shared value would have worsened.
- test_snapshot_fetch_stall_abort_12e4.py, `tight_stall`: REBAR_SNAPSHOT_STALL_WINDOW_SECONDS 2 -> 1 (the smallest value git's http.lowSpeedTime expresses; the sibling dribble test already proved git honors a 1s window).

REMOVING REAL-TIME DEPENDENCE, not just shrinking numbers. Three reap tests assert on something the child must have finished FIRST (the grandchild pidfile, the spawn counter, the flushed partial stdout); on main that ordering held only because 1s happened to exceed interpreter startup. Every hanging fake now creates a readiness file as its last act, and a parent-side Popen wrapper polls for that file before returning the process. `_run_acli` computes `call_timeout` before the loop but measures the deadline at `communicate()`, i.e. after the wrapper returns, so the injected window is spent entirely on the hang. The PID-existence checks poll to a transition via a shared `_wait_until_gone` helper under a 30s ceiling instead of the previous 5s.

WHY THESE VALUES CANNOT FLAKE ON A SLOW HOST:
- Every fake sleeps 3600s, so a SMALLER reap window makes the timeout more certain, never less: no amount of load lets the child finish first.
- Everything that could have raced the window is now gated on an observed file, not on elapsed time.
- The only remaining ceilings are hang-guards a healthy run never approaches: the 10s reap guard (~25x the 0.4s injected window, kept at 10s and NOT tightened, marker `# timing: hang-guard`), the 30s readiness/PID poll ceilings, the 30s completing-child timeout, and the unchanged 60s `_GIT_TIMEOUT` in the snapshot fixture (60x its 1s window).
- The stalled remote sends ZERO bytes, so a loaded host can delay the abort but cannot manufacture throughput above the floor; the pass condition is the failure REASON (`"stalled" in message`, `"timed out after" not in message`), never a duration.

DISCRIMINATION PROOF — ten seeded defects, each RED with the expected assertion, each reverted (`git diff -- src` clean afterwards):
- D0 terminal raise changed from AcliTimeoutError to TimeoutError -> ALL SIX reap tests RED (proves none passes vacuously).
- D1 `_reap_process_group` replaced by `p.kill(); p.wait()` (direct child only) -> test_grandchild_process_group_reaped RED: "grandchild PID 13172 survived the process-group reap".
- D2 `if retry_on_timeout and attempt < _MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1` -> `if attempt < ...` -> test_write_not_retried_on_timeout RED: "a timed-out WRITE must not be retried".
- D3 same gate forced False -> test_read_retried_then_terminal RED: "a READ should retry up to _MAX_ATTEMPTS times".
- D4 Popen `errors="replace"` -> `"strict"` -> test_truncated_utf8_does_not_crash_reap_path RED: UnicodeDecodeError.
- D5 `partial_stdout=partial_out` -> `None` -> test_partial_stdout_captured_on_timeout RED: "assert None is not None".
- D6 `_check_mutation_failure` invoked on the timeout path -> test_check_mutation_failure_not_called_on_killed_child RED.
- D7 `rl_delay = _rate_limit_backoff(...)` -> `None` -> test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff RED: "expected one Retry-After=1 backoff, got [2]".
- S1 `stall_abort_args()` -> `[]` -> test_stalled_remote_aborts_on_throughput_not_the_wall_clock RED.
- S2 floor forced to 10**9 (abort regardless of throughput = time-keyed) -> test_slow_but_progressing_remote_is_not_aborted RED: "stalled — the remote went quiet".
GREEN restored after every revert.

MEASUREMENTS (macOS, foreground): the two files 20 passed in 12.67s -> 6.13s. Per test: the five 1.01s reap tests -> 0.22s each; stalled-remote 2.06s -> 1.04s; read-retry 0.32s -> 0.66s (three ready-gated spawns; determinism deliberately bought at +0.34s); slow-progress unchanged at ~2.07s. Three consecutive clean runs at 6.44s each, then three more under 12 saturating CPU spinners on an 18-core host: 7.61s / 7.10s / 7.64s, 20 passed every time.

GATES: `make lint` PASS; `make typecheck` PASS (mypy, 582 source files); `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` -> `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`; `python scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py` -> clean; wider `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_fetch_stall_abort_12e4.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/` -> 508 passed.

comments.body: Landed. Gerrit change 1951 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1951) received LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 with zero unresolved comments and is MERGED to main as of 2026-08-20T06:49:53Z; commit 6451d3ff02 carries the rebar-ticket: baeb-4f4b-3227-457e trailer and the DCO sign-off. CI's Verified +1 ran the whole tree on the merged commit, which is the authoritative signal for this close; no local full-suite re-run was used as a gate. All seven acceptance criteria are met and ticked: the slow-progress sentinel still dribbles above the floor across a full injected 1s low-speed window and still fails only for a non-stall reason; the ACLI read sentinel still launches exactly _MAX_ATTEMPTS real child sessions and polls every recorded PID to absence; production timeout/stall/grace/drain defaults are byte-unchanged (120s/3s/2s call/grace/drain and a 10s low-speed window); both files retain real subprocess and real loopback-socket execution and now complete in 6.13s together (down from 12.67s); the single upper-bound wall-clock assertion was left at its 10s ceiling rather than tightened, and scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py reports clean; every reap assertion that depends on child-side setup is now ordered by an explicit readiness gate; and each touched sentinel was shown RED under a seeded defect and GREEN after revert (ten seeds, detailed in the preceding comment).

compiled_state.description:
## Context

This ticket was filed 45 seconds apart from `classless-dainty-lamprey` (039b-d179-b669-4439) by
the same scan and shares its title. 039b landed the FIRST pass as commit a79ed876b0: the
snapshot slow-progress test now injects a 1s low-speed window over a 2s real loopback dribble,
and the ACLI read-retry test now installs 0.1s call/grace/drain, records the logical `[2, 4]`
backoff without sleeping it, and polls every spawned PID to absence. That work is done and is
not re-litigated here.

What remains on current `origin/main` (measured, macOS, `-p no:randomly`, 20 tests / 12.67s):

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py` still carries a BLANKET
  autouse `_short_timeout` fixture that sets `REBAR_ACLI_TIMEOUT=1` plus 1s grace and 1s drain
  for the whole module. Five real-subprocess reap tests each burn ~1.01s of pure wall-clock
  waiting for that deadline to expire: `test_grandchild_process_group_reaped`,
  `test_write_not_retried_on_timeout`, `test_truncated_utf8_does_not_crash_reap_path`,
  `test_partial_stdout_captured_on_timeout`,
  `test_check_mutation_failure_not_called_on_killed_child`.
- The same blanket fixture also caps `test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff`, whose
  fake child must COMPLETE (two sequential `python -c` spawns) inside that 1s. That is a latent
  load flake in the opposite direction, and naively shrinking the module-wide value would make
  it worse — so the fixture must be split, not merely retuned.
- `tests/unit/test_snapshot_fetch_stall_abort_12e4.py`'s `tight_stall` fixture still injects a
  2s low-speed window (`test_stalled_remote_aborts_on_throughput_not_the_wall_clock`, ~2.06s)
  even though its sibling dribble test already demonstrates that git honors a 1s window.

The residual coupling is not only "the numbers are large". Three of the reap tests assert on
something the child must have DONE before the deadline fires (a grandchild pidfile, a spawn
counter, flushed partial stdout). Today the ordering holds only because 1s happens to exceed
interpreter startup — a wall-clock race that a smaller window would lose on a loaded runner.
The fix is to make the ordering explicit rather than to pick a luckier number.

## Plan

1. Split the blanket autouse `_short_timeout` fixture into two opt-in fixtures in
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py`, both driving only the
   existing test seams (`_acli_call_timeout`, `_ACLI_GRACE_SECONDS`, `_ACLI_DRAIN_SECONDS`) and
   changing no production default:
   - a reap-timing fixture installing sub-second call/grace/drain for the tests whose child is
     required to HANG (a shorter deadline makes a hang MORE certain, never less);
   - a generous hang-guard ceiling, far above any healthy run, for the tests whose child is
     required to COMPLETE, so their pass condition stops depending on runner speed at all.
2. Close the setup race instead of tuning around it. Every fake `python -c` binary writes a
   readiness marker as its LAST action before hanging, and a parent-side `Popen` wrapper polls
   for that marker (generous ceiling; early-out if the child exits) before handing the process
   back. Because `_run_acli` measures its deadline at `communicate()`, which runs after the
   wrapper returns, the injected window is spent entirely on the hang and can no longer
   pre-empt the child's setup — on any host, at any load.
3. Lower the injected low-speed window in `tight_stall` from 2s to 1s in
   `tests/unit/test_snapshot_fetch_stall_abort_12e4.py`. The abort remains throughput-keyed and
   the assertions remain reason-keyed (`"stalled" in message`, `"timed out after" not in
   message`) under an unchanged 60s `_GIT_TIMEOUT` ceiling, so a slow host makes the test
   slower, never red.
4. Prove each touched sentinel still discriminates by seeding the defect it guards (restore the
   production-scale window; disable the process-group reap; disable the timeout) and recording
   RED, then reverting and recording GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Slow-progress still crosses a full configured low-speed window and proves throughput, not elapsed wall time, prevents abort.
- [x] ACLI read still spawns exactly the production retry count and proves every process group is reaped.
- [x] Production timeout/stall defaults are unchanged.
- [x] The focused tests retain real subprocess/socket execution but complete in low single-digit seconds on macOS CI.
- [x] No absolute upper-bound assertion is tightened into a loaded-runner flake.
- [x] Every reap assertion that depends on child-side setup is ordered by an explicit readiness gate rather than by the injected window being larger than interpreter startup.
- [x] Each touched sentinel is shown RED under a seeded defect and GREEN after revert.

## File impact

- `tests/unit/test_snapshot_fetch_stall_abort_12e4.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py`

file_impact.reason: Reduce only the test-owned slow-progress window while preserving real socket throughput semantics.
Reduce only injected test timing windows while preserving retry-count and process-group reaping assertions.
